module8: Capstone: run a small company for a month
Bring every module together. You set up a practice company, run a month of real-style work, close the books and show your results to others.
Plan the company: products, customers, suppliers, tax and the apps you need.
Run a month of work: at least 15 sales, 8 purchases, 2 stock counts and one bank statement.
Close the month: reconcile the bank, check stock against the books and print the tax report.
Present your results and explain one mistake you made and how you fixed it.

A learner sells 18 orders, makes 8 purchases and reconciles 25 bank lines. The stock report shows 3 units short, which turns out to be a missed receipt. After posting the receipt, stock and books agree.
Complete the one-month practice company and write a two-page report with a screenshot of each main report, the issues found and your fixes.
Month closed with zero unreconciled bank lines, stock matching the count, and a clear written explanation of each issue.
quiz: A small shop wants to sell, track stock and keep accounts. Which apps would you install first and why?
Sales, inventory and accounting, because they cover the daily work. Add other apps later only when there is a real need.
A shirt comes in three sizes and two colours. How should you set it up?
Create one product with variants for size and colour, giving six combinations. This keeps one set of reports instead of six separate products.
You import 20 products and find 3 duplicates. What check should have been done before import?
Compare names or codes with the existing list and clean the sheet first. Also check units and tax columns before loading.
A quote is confirmed. What usually follows in the sales flow?
A delivery is made, an invoice is created from the order and then payment is registered. Each step is linked to the one before.
An invoice has payment terms of Net 30. What does that mean?
The customer should pay within 30 days of the invoice date. The due date on the invoice is set automatically from this.
A product has a minimum of 10 and a maximum of 40 in its reorder rule. Stock falls to 8. What happens?
A purchase request is created to bring stock up to the maximum, so about 32 units are suggested. The buyer reviews it before ordering.
Twenty bank lines were imported and 18 matched. What do you do with the other two?
Open each one and find the invoice or bill it belongs to, or create the missing entry. The target is zero unreconciled lines.
Why should a web shop and a physical shop use the same stock?
Both sales reduce the same quantity, so you do not sell items you no longer have. Reports also show true totals.
Before upgrading the live system, what should you do?
Take a backup and run the upgrade on a copy first. If the copy fails you still have the working live system and a way back.
Compare the work in a capstone month with a go-live plan.
A capstone month tests that you can run all daily work and close the books. A go-live plan prepares moving a real company, with backup, test, rollback and support.
ladder: L1 Basic: know the apps
Remember the main apps and what each is for. Identify the company, the current user and the access rights. Recognise a customer, a product and an order on screen.
Show the app list and ask learners which they need for a shop. Check they can find their own company name. A common mistake is installing every app at once.
L2 Awareness: see the flow
Understand how a sale links to stock and to the invoice. Explain why clean product and customer data matters. Describe the idea of a chart of accounts and bank matching.
Draw the flow with arrows from quote to payment. Ask where stock changes. Watch for learners who think each app keeps separate numbers.
L3 Foundation: enter daily work
Apply the steps to create contacts, products, quotes, orders and invoices. Register a payment. Use filters and search to find a record.
Let learners enter five orders. Check each is invoiced and paid. Common mistake: typing a new customer when one already exists.
L4 Practitioner: run stock and buying
Apply reorder rules, purchase orders and stock counts. Analyse a stock difference and post an adjustment with a reason. Check the stock value against the books.
Plant one missed receipt in the practice data. Ask learners to find it. Common mistake: forcing the count to agree without finding the cause.
L5 Specialist: close the books
Analyse bank lines and match them to invoices and bills. Evaluate whether the tax report is correct. Fix wrong entries in a safe way.
Give a bank file with two odd lines. Check learners explain each one. Common mistake: matching to the nearest amount instead of the true document.
L6 Advanced: build and automate
Create a test shop page and simple automated actions that save time. Evaluate changes made with the studio tool against changes made with code. Keep every change in a test copy first.
Ask learners to show a change on the copy and then on live. Check they can name the risk. Common mistake: editing the live system directly.
L7 Super expert: lead the rollout
Create a go-live plan with migration, backups, rehearsal, rollback and support. Evaluate trade-offs for a real small company. Teach a team to run the system.
Ask learners to present a plan to a peer who plays the owner. Check the backup and rollback steps. Common mistake: moving all data in one step with no rehearsal.
